Get trained to document local government meetings and get involved in Detroit 

Learn to research and monitor public officials, check out nature-based STEM careers, experience a glowing night hike and more.
by Lynelle Herndon August 19, 2026August 18, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
0:00 / 9:07
Instaread

From trainings to volunteering and paid gigs, find opportunities to get involved in Detroit every week — brought to you by the Detroit Documenters. 

Hey, Detroit! 

If you missed our orientation yesterday, don’t worry. You can hang out with Documenters at the Crowell Recreation Center tomorrow to learn more, and join our virtual orientation on Aug. 26 to get certified to take paid assignments documenting local government meetings. 

There are also some fun science and nature events happening next week. Girls ages 10-16 are invited to explore nature-based STEM careers on Tuesday, and everyone is invited to take a “glowing” night hike on Belle Isle on Aug. 27. 

Creative writers are invited to a collective working session at the Detroit Public Theatre (DPT) on Aug. 26. DPT is also hiring an associate production manager and a box office associate. You can also watch free shows when you volunteer as an usher. 

Aspiring Black writers are invited to find their voice at a writer’s workshop on Sept. 5. 

The last few weeks of summer offer a little something for everyone to get involved! 

Happening soon 

Meet Documenters in the Park
Thursday, Aug. 20, 6-8 p.m.
Crowell Recreation Center, 16630 Lahser Road, Detroit
Bring your family or friends to hang out with Detroit Documenters at the Crowell Rec Center playground, north of the Brightmoor neighborhood. Look for the yellow Documenters banner. 

Power Researching Elected Officials
Thursday, Aug. 20, 7-8:30 p.m.
Online
Learn to research the relationships between elected officials and their campaign donors with a free training from LittleSis. Register now. 

Become a Detroit Documenter

Outlier Media’s Documenters program trains and pays Detroiters to attend local public meetings and monitor our elected officials, in collaboration with local journalists. Join the Documenters network to get involved!

Stream Girls Career Day
Tuesday, Aug. 25, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
Fort Street Bridge Interpretive Park, 12700 Denmark St., Detroit

Girls ages 10-16 are invited to participate in fun and educational environmental science activities designed to promote a career in science, technology, engineering or math. Learn more and register now.

In the Process
Wednesday, Aug. 26, 5-7 p.m.
Detroit Public Theatre, 3960 Third St., Detroit
Get in your creative flow with a collective work session led by Danielle Eliska at DPT. Register now.

Detroit Documenters Virtual Orientation
Wednesday, Aug. 26, 6-8 p.m.
Online
Get trained to take paid assignments documenting local public meetings. Register now. 

Nature at Night: UV Gotta See This
Thursday, Aug. 27, 8-10 p.m.
Belle Isle Nature Center, 176 Lakeside Dr., Detroit
The glow of a UV light reveals the invisible fluorescent patterns of certain plants and animals. Following an engaging presentation from Joseph Ferraro on the science of fluorescence in nature, participants will take a guided night hike to explore the phenomenon for themselves. Admission is free and no registration is required. 

Black Writers Salon
Saturday, Sept. 5, 1-4 p.m.
Chai Khana, 3574 Second Ave., Detroit
Award-winning writer, community builder (and Detroit Documenter!) Ru Colvin hosts a generative writing workshop to help you find your voice at the Late Fee Collective’s fifth writing salon. RSVP for your seat.

Now hiring 

Box Office Associate
Detroit Public Theatre is hiring someone to manage the box office for its 12th season from September to June. The part-time position pays $15.50 an hour. Learn more and fill out the form to apply.

Associate Production Manager
Detroit Public Theatre is hiring someone to oversee the technical elements of productions. The full-time position pays a salary of $45,000 plus benefits. Learn more about the job and qualifications. Then send a résumé, cover letter and supporting materials to employment@detroitpublictheatre.org with “APM APPLICATION” in the subject line. 

Senior Director of Land Use and Community Leadership
Urban Neighborhood Initiatives is seeking someone to lead urban planning and youth engagement efforts in Southwest Detroit’s Springwells neighborhood. The full-time position pays a salary of $58,000-$68,000 plus benefits. Learn more about the job responsibilities and qualifications. Then, email your résumé and cover letter to Christine Bell at hr@unidetroit.org. 

Staff Attorney
The Detroit Justice Center is hiring an attorney to help advance the legal nonprofit’s mission of criminal justice reform and civil rights advocacy. The full-time hybrid position pays a salary of $85,000-$90,000 plus benefits, with a start date of Sept. 1. Apply now. 

Electoral Canvasser
Detroit Action is hiring people to talk to residents about current issues and voter registration for November’s general election. Canvassers are paid $22 an hour. Learn more and apply now. 

Director of External Affairs & Communications
Michigan Community Resources is hiring someone to manage its public engagement. Salary for the full-time position starts at $80,000 plus benefits. Learn more about the position and apply now. 

Senior Analyst
Data Driven Detroit is hiring a researcher to support and coordinate two programs, tracking neighborhood conditions and promoting early childhood services. This full-time, remote position offers a starting salary of $60,000, 32-hour workweeks and benefits. Apply now. 

Communications Director
Rising Voices, a Detroit nonprofit organizing Asians and Pacific Islanders in Michigan, is hiring someone to lead its communications strategy. They will also oversee press relations and Michigan voter engagement efforts. This hybrid position offers a salary of $63,750-$85,000, health coverage and more benefits. Apply now. 

Evergreen opportunities 

Volunteer Usher
Detroit Public Theatre needs ushers this season. These volunteers can watch the shows they help with or get free tickets. Learn more and sign up now!

Volunteer With a Chess Club
The Wise Guys Chess Club is seeking volunteers to help with everything from coaching to youth mentoring, including graphic design, social media work and more. Sign up now to help empower the next generation of thinkers. 

Bookapalooza
Making Spirits Bright is offering free books for families and nonprofit organizations. Sign up to get your free books! Pickup will be in Plymouth. You can also donate books, host a book drive or volunteer to sort and distribute books. 

Belle Isle Cleanup Crew
Help “Keep Belle Isle Beautiful” and volunteer to clean up the beach on Friday, Sept. 11. Volunteers can also clean up the land and water on Saturday, Sept. 19. No registration is needed, but a volunteer waiver is required. 

Ecorse Creek Cleanup
Friends of the Detroit River is hosting cleanups of Ecorse Creek at different locations on the second Saturday of the month through September. All cleanup supplies are provided. Get more information and register to volunteer. 

We Walk Detroit
Join a walking group and exercise with friends. Through September, meet up for a one-hour walk at eight city parks, the Joe Louis Greenway and the riverfront. All participants get a T-shirt. Check out the schedule. 

WTF Night at Back Alley Bikes
Women, trans, femme and other gender minorities are invited to fix up their ride at Back Alley Bikes’ open workshop every third Wednesday of the month, from 5-8 p.m., behind The Hub at 3611 Cass Ave., Detroit. 

Immigration Office Hours
Detroit People’s Assembly offers help with urgent immigration paperwork, including bond requests, stays of removal, temporary protected status filings and work permits. Office hours are 5-8 p.m. Thursdays at Grace in Action Church, 1725 Lawndale St., Detroit. 

Become an Immigration Court Observer
The American Bar Association’s Commission on Immigration will train you to volunteer as an immigration court observer. Learn firsthand about the immigration court system while helping identify patterns that will inform advocacy and support access to counsel and due process rights for noncitizens. Enroll now. 

Free Tutoring
PrepandMe helps students prepare for college, leadership and lifelong success. The free program offers tutoring and standardized test preparation, college counseling, a device to access online applications, a $1,000 annual stipend, college tours, summer programming and more. The organization is currently accepting rising eighth graders with a 3.0 grade point average for sessions starting this fall. Teachers can recommend students. Families must meet household income eligibility criteria. Learn more and apply now. 

Free Computer Classes
Detroit Public Library offers a wide range of computer- and technology-related classes for all ages — from basic computer skills and troubleshooting your phone or internet to classes in productivity and graphic design software. Find free group and individual support at multiple library branches. 

Free Health Screenings
Wayne Health’s mobile units deliver health care and social services directly to neighborhoods and places of employment. Teams of registered nurses and other medical professionals offer screenings for things such as high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol and kidney disease, as well as COVID-19 testing and vaccines. They can also connect you with mental health resources. To see when they’ll be in your neighborhood, view the event calendar. 

Education Survey
Education policy is a critical issue for Michigan’s next governor. Chalkbeat Detroit and the Detroit Free Press are teaming up to learn metro Detroiters’ priorities. Take the survey. 

Youth Engagement Survey
BridgeDetroit seeks to connect with local high school students ages 13-18 to understand how they consume news, what issues matter to them and how they want to engage civically. The survey will inform BridgeDetroit’s coverage and events. Learn more and take the survey. 

Join The Outlier Collective
If you care about your city and strive to make it better, consider joining The Outlier Collective for exclusive events, service opportunities and more. Support Outlier Media’s investigative reporting and work to inform and empower Detroiters. Join now. 

Support Detroit journalism that serves you

Our reporting for Detroiters is free because readers like you make it possible. Your donation powers independent, local journalism that holds institutions accountable and empowers your neighbors. If you value this work, please consider giving today — your support ensures these stories continue, for everyone.

Detroit Documenters Orientation is today!

Enjoy music, food, conversation, health, legal resources and more at the Black Legacy Advancement Coalition’s annual celebration.

Boost your civic résumé and get involved in Detroit

Take a harm reduction workshop Thursday, and learn to perfect your public comment in a Petty Propolis workshop.

Meet Nick Kramer, this month’s featured Detroit Documenter

Covering local public meetings satisfied his civic curiosity. He never imagined he’d be featured as a Detroit Documenter.
